items.label: Pain
items.description: Students discover citation problems too late.

items.label: Input
items.description: The fastest flow for a Vibe Coding demo.

items.label: Output
items.description: A ranked list of references to verify first.

checklist: Extract the bibliography from References or Bibliography sections
Flag citations without DOI, URL, or source trail evidence
Spot unknown publication dates and weak venue signals
Summarize risky, review-needed, and trusted references
audit.sample_manuscript:
This draft discusses retrieval-augmented writing and cites Smith (2024), Wang (n.d.), and Patel (2020).

References
[1] Smith, J. (2024). Verified citation. Journal of AI, 12(2), 30-44. https://doi.org/10.1000/demo
[2] Wang, L. (n.d.). AI assisted writing habits. Retrieved from example.com
[3] Patel, R. (2020). Missing source trail for a citation.

introduce.title: Citation checking is a real student workflow, not a toy problem
introduce.description: When students write papers, they often need to know whether cited sources actually look traceable. CiteTrace turns that anxiety into a focused review step before submission.

faq.title: Questions about the first version
faq.description: The MVP is intentionally narrow so it can be shipped and evaluated quickly.

items.question: Does this prove whether a paper source is real?
items.answer: Not yet. This MVP performs a first-pass source-trail audit. It flags weak references and gives students a repair queue. A later version can call LLM, Crossref, Google Scholar-like search, or library APIs for stronger verification.

items.question: Why not build full PDF parsing immediately?
items.answer: The first demo keeps the input to paste or plain text upload so the product value is visible fast. PDF and DOCX parsing are natural follow-up integrations.

items.question: What makes this a good Vibe Coding project?
items.answer: It starts from a real pain point, has a small interaction loop, shows PM-style scoping, and can be expanded with AI retrieval after the landing page and UX prove the value.

items.question: Can this become a paid SaaS?
items.answer: Yes. The likely paid layer is batch uploads, institutional accounts, stronger source lookup, exportable reports, and LMS integrations.
